title: Emergency runtime patch: KV-cache corruption + GPU OOMs across Hosted/Dedicated/Private
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Summary:
Multiple customers reported production incidents between 2026-02-25 and 2026-03-01: large hosted deployments and some Dedicated/Private nodes experienced sudden GPU OOMs and degraded throughput. Post-incident correlation points to two related runtime problems: a KV-cache reference-counting leak/corruption that allows stale pointers into GPU-resident tensors, and progressive memory fragmentation on long-running processes that magnifies OOM risk under load. This ticket tracks the emergency investigation, the runtime patch, rollout plan, and follow-ups.

Incident details and evidence:
- Customer A (hosted, us-west-2) saw repeated model worker restarts and OOMs during long chat sessions. Crash logs: gpu_mem_overcommit + invalid GPU pointer deref at kv_cache.cpp:412.
- Customer B (dedicated) had a slow memory growth over 48h, culminating in OOM while dumping activations. Heap snapshots show many small pinned allocations and fragmented free lists.
- Customer C (private, on-prem) reported KV cache corruption after heavy concurrent evictions following burst traffic; observed mismatched key->tensor mappings.
- Commonalities: (1) heavy reuse of KV cache and short-lived conversation prefixes, (2) mixed request size distribution causing many small allocations, (3) higher concurrency during peak.

Reproduction steps (dev/stress):
1. Run repro harness: stress/repro_gpu_kvcache.py against local runtime with --concurrency 128 --seq-dist heavy-tail --evict-burst 20.
2. Enable debug kv logging and set KV_CACHE_EPOCH=1 to reproduce stale pointer path.
3. Run fragmented_allocator_test with small chunk size to emulate long-running fragmentation.
Observed: pointer invalidation race after concurrent promote+evict, and allocator free lists split across many small spans.

Root cause hypothesis (confirmed by added debug traces and memory snapshots):
- KV-cache: Concurrent promote path does an unchecked pointer handoff when a hot entry is re-pointed into a new GPU tensor. Under concurrent evict/promote the old entry could be freed while another thread still held a transient pointer -> use-after-free/corruption that triggers OOM or invalid access in GPU allocator. Missing epoch guard on GPU pointer lifetime.
- Memory fragmentation: our pinned allocator favors allocating small pinned tensors in separate GPU blocks; repeated allocate/free without compaction leads to fragmentation and inability to satisfy large contiguous allocation requests (model context or kv materialization) despite nominal free memory.

Immediate mitigations applied (already deployed to hosted canaries):
- Hotfix PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4023 implementing epoch-based KV entry invalidation and atomic pointer swap with refcount increment.
- Temporary config changes: reduced default pin_threshold from 64KB to 256KB on hosted worker pools to reduce small pinned allocations.
- Autoscaler emergency: increase Dedicated burst capacity policy for impacted customers to provide headroom while patch rolls out.
- Fallback route: route heavy request sequences to quantized-model variant (quant-q4f) for customers with tolerable quality delta.

Proposed permanent fixes (this ticket will track work until complete):
1) Apply epoch/ownership model to KV cache with safe reclamation window; add per-entry epoch and atomic acquire semantics.
2) Add background compaction path for pinned allocator: coalesce small pinned tensors into larger contiguous blocks when fragmentation threshold exceeded.
3) Improve eviction path to avoid promoting entries under active concurrent mutate; add explicit promotion handshake.
4) Add stress tests to CI that simulate concurrency + eviction beyond previous coverage.
5) Add metrics and alerts: kv_cache_live_handles, kv_cache_failed_acquires, pinned_fragmentation_ratio, allocator_max_span_request_failures.

Testing and verification plan:
- Unit/regression: new tests in tests/kv_cache_concurrency_test.cpp and tests/pinned_compaction_test.cpp.
- Integration stress: run canary cluster for 72h with stress harness targeting previously failing scenarios; require zero invalid-ptr traces and <1% increase in tail latency.
- Customer validation: coordinate with top-affected customers to run their workload in canary (Customer A and B agreed).

Rollout plan (sensible for Hosted/Dedicated/Private):
- Step 1 (Canary Hosted): Deploy runtime-2.3.1-patch to us-west-2 hosted workers at 1% traffic (03/04). Monitor kv metrics for 48h.
- Step 2 (Extended Canary): Increase to 10% (03/06) if stable. Targeted Dedicated test clusters enabled.
- Step 3 (Selective Dedicated): Offer patch to Dedicated clusters for customers with maintenance window; apply with 1-hour drain and health-check gating.
- Step 4 (Private): Provide binary + patch notes and coordinate on-prem upgrades with SE; do not auto-upgrade private installations.
- Step 5 (Full rollout): 100% hosted by 03/13 if all checks green; Dedicated rollout completed by 03/15 pending customer windows.

Monitoring and alerting to add before full rollout:
- Grafana dashboard: runtime/kv-cache/ownership-latency, runtime/gpu/allocator-frag, runtime/kv-cache/failed-promotes.
- Pager rule: kv_cache_failed_acquires > 5/min for 5m in production triggers on-call.

Communication and customer handling:
- On 2026-03-02 SRE sent interim remediation to Customer A and B outlining mitigations and temporary capacity bump.
- Postfix: committed to a transparent postmortem and remediation timeline; CS/SE reps assigned for each impacted account: Customer A -> Priya Singh, Customer B -> Tom Novak.

Next steps (owners):
- Merge hotfix PR and tag release (owner: Luca Ramirez, ETA 2026-03-03).
- Run 72h canary stress and report (owner: QA - Andres Park, ETA 2026-03-08).
- Add new metrics & dashboard (owner: Observability - Zoe Carter, ETA 2026-03-07).
- Plan compaction work and design doc (owner: Eng - Maya Chen, ETA 2026-03-20).

Postmortem checklist (post-resolution):
- Root-cause writeup and timeline.
- Customer impact summary and credits if applicable.
- Retro on testing coverage gaps and CI stress scenarios.
- Schedule follow-up EPIC for allocator compaction and KV-cache concurrency redesign.
